correctness.rationale: With M>=2, sorted distinct 0<r_i<1, unit recovery, and s_i>0, the polynomial q(x)=(1-x)P(x)-1 has degree M, q(1)=-1, so all prescribed M roots force q(x)=-prod(x-r_i)/prod(1-r_i), uniquely. The penultimate rate lambda_(M-1)=(1-sum r_i)/D forces the strict root-sum inequality. Under sum<1, elementary symmetric functions obey (k+1)e_(k+1)<=S e_k, so their alternating partial sums are positive and every reconstructed rate is strictly positive. The exact factorization verifies the roots, no others, and linearization signs. Reconstructed independent standard-library rational checker passed 2,338 families, 18,718 root evaluations across M<=15 including sharp equality and inadmissibility examples. No finite experiment is treated as proof of all-orders result.

value.rationale: The earlier literature motivates multistable endemic regimes but does not specify which collections of distinct prevalence levels can be produced by physically admissible strictly positive group-contagion rates. A full exact inverse characterization is a natural parameter-design question, and the single sharp constraint sum(r_i)<1 with explicit unique rates supplies both nontrivial impossibility and complete constructive feasibility at every order. It is informative beyond a special numerical example, root-count upper bound, or textbook rate expansion. Scientific limits are fixed-order homogeneous mean-field equations and complete distinct-root prescriptions.
